title: Ancient Pilbara reshapes understanding of the Earth
description: Researchers believe an early Earth process known as “dripduction” may have transported water-rich crust into the mantle before modern plate tectonics developed. Image: Kings Access/stock.adobe.com New research challenges long-held assumptions about the planet’s earliest geological processes. A new study examining 3.1-billion-year-old volcanic rocks from Western Australia’s Pilbara Craton has found evidence that water was already being transported deep into Earth’s interior long before modern plate tectonics developed.
